claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic screen studies.

claims.claim: Auditory hair cells are sensory receptor cells that convert acoustic and mechanical stimuli into electrical signals initiating hearing.
claims.source: The auditory hair cells are the sensory receptor cells that convert acoustic and mechanical stimuli into electrical signals initiating hearing (Fettiplace, 2017; Hudspeth, 1989; Ó Maoiléidigh and Ricci, 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on hair cell function.

claims.claim: The hair bundle is a specialized organelle situated at the apical surface of each hair cell.
claims.source: The hair bundle, a specialized organelle situated at the apical surface of each hair cell, responds to mechanical displacement in a direction-dependent manner (Flock, 1964; Tilney et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational studies on hair bundle structure.

claims.claim: The hair bundle responds to mechanical displacement in a direction-dependent manner.
claims.source: The hair bundle, a specialized organelle situated at the apical surface of each hair cell, responds to mechanical displacement in a direction-dependent manner (Flock, 1964; Tilney et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational studies on hair bundle function.

claims.claim: The hair bundle is essential for mechanoelectrical transduction (MET).
claims.source: The hair bundle is essential for mechanoelectrical transduction (MET), and defects in the hair bundle can cause hearing loss (Belyantseva et al., 2009; Blanco-Sánchez et al., 2014; Kozlov et al., 2007; Noben-Trauth et al., 2003; Perrin et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies linking hair bundle defects to hearing loss.

claims.claim: Defects in the hair bundle can cause hearing loss.
claims.source: The hair bundle is essential for mechanoelectrical transduction (MET), and defects in the hair bundle can cause hearing loss (Belyantseva et al., 2009; Blanco-Sánchez et al., 2014; Kozlov et al., 2007; Noben-Trauth et al., 2003; Perrin et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies demonstrating this relationship.

claims.claim: Several proteins are required for the morphogenesis and physiological regulation of the hair bundle.
claims.source: Several proteins, such as adhesion molecules, actin-bundling proteins, and disease-associated proteins are required for the morphogenesis and physiological regulation of the hair bundle (Barr-Gillespie, 2015; Blanco-Sánchez et al., 2017; McGrath et al., 2017; Tilney et al., 1980).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on hair bundle proteins.

claims.claim: Specific lipid molecules may play a role in the hair bundle.
claims.source: In addition, specific lipid molecules may play a role in the hair bundle.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by subsequent examples of PIP2 function in hair bundles.

claims.claim: Phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is localized to hair bundles.
claims.source: For instance, phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is localized to hair bundles, and it binds to the MET channel component TMIE (Cunningham et al., 2020) and regulates the rates of fast and slow adaptation (Effertz et al., 2017; Hirono et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on PIP2 localization and function.

claims.claim: PIP2 binds to the MET channel component TMIE.
claims.source: For instance, phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is localized to hair bundles, and it binds to the MET channel component TMIE (Cunningham et al., 2020) and regulates the rates of fast and slow adaptation (Effertz et al., 2017; Hirono et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2020.

claims.claim: PIP2 regulates the rates of fast and slow adaptation in hair cells.
claims.source: For instance, phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is localized to hair bundles, and it binds to the MET channel component TMIE (Cunningham et al., 2020) and regulates the rates of fast and slow adaptation (Effertz et al., 2017; Hirono et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Effertz et al., 2017 and Hirono et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Cholesterol is an important component of eukaryotic cell membranes.
claims.source: Cholesterol is an important component of eukaryotic cell membranes, and it controls membrane stiffness, tension, fluidity, and other membrane properties (Maxfield and van Meer, 2010; Subczynski et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on cholesterol function.

claims.claim: Cholesterol controls membrane stiffness, tension, fluidity, and other membrane properties.
claims.source: Cholesterol is an important component of eukaryotic cell membranes, and it controls membrane stiffness, tension, fluidity, and other membrane properties (Maxfield and van Meer, 2010; Subczynski et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on cholesterol's effects on membrane properties.

claims.claim: Cholesterol plays a regulatory function by interacting with membrane proteins.
claims.source: Cholesterol also plays a regulatory function by interacting with membrane proteins (Harris, 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Harris, 2010.

claims.claim: Abnormally high or low cholesterol levels are detrimental to hearing.
claims.source: Previous studies showed that abnormally high or low cholesterol levels are detrimental to hearing (Corwin and Warchol, 1991; Crumling et al., 2012; Ding et al., 2020; Guo et al., 2005; King et al., 2014a; King et al., 2014b; Morizono and Paparella, 1978; Sikora et al., 1986; Takahashi et al., 2016; Thoenes et al., 2015; Xing et al., 2015; Yao et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on cholesterol and hearing.

claims.claim: Cholesterol is not uniformly distributed in hair cell membranes.
claims.source: Early studies also showed that cholesterol is not uniformly distributed in the hair cell membranes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by subsequent citations to studies showing differential cholesterol distribution.

claims.claim: The intensities of cholesterol labeling in hair cells are higher in the apical membranes compared to the lateral membranes.
claims.source: The intensities of cholesterol labeling the hair cells were higher in the apical membranes when compared to those of the lateral membranes (Nguyen and Brownell, 1998; Takahashi et al., 2016), and freeze-fracture images of hair cells suggested that the stereocilia membrane was densely covered with cholesterol (Forge et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nguyen and Brownell, 1998 and Takahashi et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Freeze-fracture images of hair cells suggest that the stereocilia membrane is densely covered with cholesterol.
claims.source: The intensities of cholesterol labeling the hair cells were higher in the apical membranes when compared to those of the lateral membranes (Nguyen and Brownell, 1998; Takahashi et al., 2016), and freeze-fracture images of hair cells suggested that the stereocilia membrane was densely covered with cholesterol (Forge et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Forge et al., 1988.

claims.claim: The distribution of cholesterol in hair cells in vivo is not well characterized.
claims.source: Nevertheless, the distribution of cholesterol in hair cells in vivo, and cholesterol's functional role in hair cells are not well characterized.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on the authors' assessment of the existing literature.

claims.claim: Cholesterol's functional role in hair cells is not well characterized.
claims.source: Nevertheless, the distribution of cholesterol in hair cells in vivo, and cholesterol's functional role in hair cells are not well characterized.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on the authors' assessment of the existing literature.

claims.claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 was identified in a hearing loss screen in mouse knockout strains using the auditory brainstem response test.
claims.source: Kiaa1024L/Minar2, a previously understudied gene, was identified in a hearing loss screen in mouse knockout strains using the auditory brainstem response test.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bowl et al., 2017 and Ingham et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Homozygous Kiaa1024L/Minar2 knockout mice aged 14 weeks old had severely raised ABR thresholds at all frequencies tested.
claims.source: The homozygous Kiaa1024L/Minar2 knockout mice aged 14 weeks old had severely raised ABR thresholds at all frequencies tested (Bowl et al., 2017; Ingham et al., 2019), but how Kiaa1024L/Minar2 functioned in the hearing was unclear.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bowl et al., 2017 and Ingham et al., 2019.

claims.claim: kiaa1024L/minar2 is expressed in zebrafish mechanosensory hair cells.
claims.source: Here we show kiaa1024L/minar2 is expressed in the zebrafish mechanosensory hair cells, and disruption of kiaa1024L/minar2 causes hearing loss in the zebrafish larvae.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: GFP or FLAG-tagged Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein is distributed in the stereocilia and the apical endo-membranes.
claims.source: We next show that GFP or FLAG-tagged Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein is distributed in the stereocilia and the apical endo-membranes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein is mainly localized to lysosomes in cultured cells.
claims.source: In vitro studies in cultured cells show that the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein is mainly localized to lysosomes, and overexpression of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 recruits cholesterol and results in increased intracellular cholesterol levels.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-D.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 recruits cholesterol and results in increased intracellular cholesterol levels.
claims.source: In vitro studies in cultured cells show that the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein is mainly localized to lysosomes, and overexpression of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 recruits cholesterol and results in increased intracellular cholesterol levels.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by filipin staining data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Treatment that raises cholesterol levels rescues hair cell defects and hearing in the mutant kiaa1024L/minar2 larvae.
claims.source: Drug treatment that lowers cholesterol levels aggravates, whereas treatment that raises cholesterol levels rescues hair cell defects and hearing in the mutant kiaa1024L/minar2 larvae.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by efavirenz and voriconazole treatment data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Kiaa1024L/minar2 gene orthologs are found in vertebrate species only.
claims.source: Kiaa1024L/minar2 gene orthologs are found in vertebrate species only (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: There are two kiaa1024/minar1/ubtor gene orthologs in the zebrafish genome.

claims.claim: There is a single kiaa1024l/minar2 gene ortholog in the zebrafish genome.

claims.evidence: This claim is based on genome annotation analysis and BLAST searches.

claims.claim: The transcripts of minar2 orthologs are highly enriched in the auditory hair cells of the mouse and the zebrafish.
claims.source: We surveyed available sequencing data (Barta et al., 2018; Elkon et al., 2015; Erickson and Nicolson, 2015; Liu et al., 2018) and found the transcripts of minar2 orthologs were highly enriched in the auditory hair cells of the mouse and the zebrafish (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: MINAR2 is specifically expressed in differentiated hair cells in a human inner ear organoid model.
claims.source: In a human inner ear organoid model (Steinhart et al., 2022), MINAR2 is specifically expressed in differentiated hair cells, similar to known differentiated hair cell markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of data from Steinhart et al., 2022 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The mutation in the minar2fs139 allele is a 5 bp deletion in exon 1.
claims.source: The mutation in the minar2fs139 allele was a 5 bp deletion in exon 1, and in the minar2fs140 allele was a 5 bp insertion in exon 1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The mutation in the minar2fs140 allele is a 5 bp insertion in exon 1.
claims.source: The mutation in the minar2fs139 allele was a 5 bp deletion in exon 1, and in the minar2fs140 allele was a 5 bp insertion in exon 1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Both minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 mutations are frameshift mutations that lead to premature termination of protein translation.
claims.source: Both mutations were frameshift mutations and led to premature termination of protein translation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the nature of the mutations (5 bp deletion/insertion) and their effects on the reading frame.

claims.claim: The mutant Minar2 proteins lack the transmembrane helix located at the carboxyl terminus.
claims.source: The translatable protein sequence in either mutant was very short and lacked the transmembrane helix located at the carboxyl terminus of the protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the predicted protein sequences shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The mutant Minar2fs139 protein is predicted to translate to the 25th amino acid, then adds 28 code-shifted residues before the reading frame stops.
claims.source: The mutant Minar2fs139 protein was predicted to translate to the 25th amino acid, then adds 28 code-shifted residues before the reading frame stopped.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on computational prediction of the mutant protein sequence.

claims.claim: The mutant Minar2fs140 protein is predicted to translate to the 26th amino acid, then adds 55 code-shifted residues.
claims.source: The mutant Minar2fs140 protein was predicted to translate to the 26th amino acid, then adds 55 code-shifted residues.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on computational prediction of the mutant protein sequence.

claims.claim: Both minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 mutants are expected to be loss of function alleles.
claims.source: Thus, both mutants were expected to be loss of function alleles.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the severe truncation of the predicted protein products.

claims.claim: The expression levels of minar2 in the two mutants are markedly down-regulated in the developing zebrafish.
claims.source: In addition, quantitative PCR analyses showed the expression levels of minar2 in the two mutants were markedly down-regulated in the developing zebrafish, most likely because the premature translational terminations activated the nonsense-mediated mRNA decays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The premature translational terminations likely activated nonsense-mediated mRNA decay.
claims.source: In addition, quantitative PCR analyses showed the expression levels of minar2 in the two mutants were markedly down-regulated in the developing zebrafish, most likely because the premature translational terminations activated the nonsense-mediated mRNA decays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observed mRNA down-regulation and known mechanisms of nonsense-mediated decay.

claims.claim: Expression levels of ubtora/minar1a and ubtorb/minar1b are not changed in the minar2fs139 nor the minar2fs140 mutants.
claims.source: To assess if loss of minar2 resulted in genetic compensation (El-Brolosy et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2019) by upregulating kiaa1024/ubtor/minar1 gene expression, we carried out quantitative PCR and found that expression levels of ubtora/minar1a and ubtorb/minar1b were not changed in the minar2fs139 nor the minar2fs140 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The SLC response rates to a 200 Hz stimulus are significantly reduced in the minar2fs139 mutant at 8 dpf.
claims.source: We found the SLC response rates to a 200 Hz stimulus were significantly reduced in the minar2fs139 mutant at 8 dpf (Figure 1B, median response rates: 80% in the wild type, and 60% in the mutant. P<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by C-start response data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The minar2fs139 mutant has significantly elevated AEP thresholds compared with the wild type control.
claims.source: Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA revealed that the minar2fs139 mutant had significantly elevated AEP thresholds compared with the wild type control (For genotype factor, F(1, 22)=7.457, p=0.0122. For genotype x frequency, F(5, 110)=6.072, p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by AEP recording data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: The AEP thresholds are significantly higher at 100–400 Hz tone bursts in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: The AEP thresholds were significantly higher at 100–400 Hz tone bursts in the minar2fs139 mutant (for 100 Hz tone, 151.0±1.2 dB for minar2fs139, 145.7±1.4 dB for wild type control; for 200 Hz tone, 152.2±1.1 dB for minar2fs139, 145.2±2.0 dB for wild type control; for 400 Hz, 143.6±1.1 dB for minar2fs139, 138.6±1.3 dB for wild type control).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by AEP recording data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: minar2 is required for normal hearing in zebrafish larvae.
claims.source: These results indicate that minar2 is required for normal hearing in the zebrafish larvae, and together with the loss of hearing phenotype in Minar2 knockout mice (Bowl et al., 2017; Ingham et al., 2019), strengthen the conclusion that minar2 orthologs play essential roles in the auditory functions of the vertebrates.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the C-start and AEP data presented in Figure 1B-C.

claims.claim: minar2 orthologs play essential roles in the auditory functions of vertebrates.
claims.source: These results indicate that minar2 is required for normal hearing in the zebrafish larvae, and together with the loss of hearing phenotype in Minar2 knockout mice (Bowl et al., 2017; Ingham et al., 2019), strengthen the conclusion that minar2 orthologs play essential roles in the auditory functions of the vertebrates.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined evidence in zebrafish and mice.

claims.claim: The labeling intensities of AM1-43 are markedly reduced in the hair cells of the lateral line neuromasts of the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: We found the labeling intensities of AM1-43 were markedly reduced in the hair cells of the lateral line neuromasts of the minar2fs139 mutant (56.8% and 51.1% of wild-type controls at 5 dpf and 8 dpf, respectively).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by AM1-43 labeling data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: The average number of hair cells is decreased in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: The results showed the average number of hair cells was decreased in the minar2fs139 mutant (82.3% and 82.1% of wild-type controls at 5 dpf and 8 dpf, respectively).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by hair cell counting data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Loss of minar2 function mainly affects hair cell mechanotransduction in zebrafish larvae.
claims.source: Because the decreases in hair cell numbers (~18% reduction) are smaller than those reductions of AM1-43 labeling intensities (~50% reduction), these results suggest that loss of minar2 function mainly affects hair cell mechanotransduction in the zebrafish larvae.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the magnitude of hair cell loss versus AM1-43 labeling reduction.

claims.claim: Loss of minar2 does not alter the number of hair cells in the inner ears of zebrafish larvae.
claims.source: In the zebrafish larvae, loss of minar2 didn't alter the number of hair cells in the inner ears (for 5 dpf wild type: 23.9±0.6, minar2fs139 mutant: 23.6±0.4, minar2fs140 mutant: 24.9±0.6 hair cells, F(2, 82)=1.399, p=0.253; for 8 dpf wild type: 32.5±0.7, minar2fs139 mutant: 32.9±0.5, minar2fs140 mutant: 33.0±0.7 hair cells, F(2, 79)=0.2378, p=0.789, both of the lateral crista of inner ear, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by hair cell counting data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: The homozygous minar2 mutants are viable.
claims.source: The homozygous minar2 mutants were viable, and the body length and body weight of adults were no different from the wild-type controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by observation and measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The body length and body weight of adult minar2 mutants are no different from wild-type controls.
claims.source: The homozygous minar2 mutants were viable, and the body length and body weight of adults were no different from the wild-type controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The inner ear regions are smaller in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: Nevertheless, hematoxylin and eosin staining of head sections suggested the inner ear regions were smaller and the numbers of hair cells were decreased in the utricle, semicircular canal crista, and saccule of the minar2fs139 mutant (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: The numbers of hair cells are decreased in the utricle, semicircular canal crista, and saccule of the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: Nevertheless, hematoxylin and eosin staining of head sections suggested the inner ear regions were smaller and the numbers of hair cells were decreased in the utricle, semicircular canal crista, and saccule of the minar2fs139 mutant (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: The average numbers of hair cells are broadly decreased across different regions of utricles and saccules in the minar2fs139 mutant, ranging from 71.2% to 84.3% of wild-type controls.
claims.source: The average numbers of hair cells were broadly decreased across different regions of utricles and saccules in the minar2fs139 mutant, ranging from 71.2% to 84.3% of wild-type controls (Figure 1F, for the utricles, the genotype factor, F(1, 32)=37.77, p<0.0001; for the saccules, the genotype factor, F(1, 19)=19.94, p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by hair cell counting data in dissected inner ear organs shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: minar2 is required for mechanotransduction in zebrafish larvae.
claims.source: We conclude that minar2 is required for mechanotransduction in the zebrafish larvae, and loss of minar2 reduces the number of inner ear hair cells in the zebrafish adults.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by AM1-43 labeling data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Loss of minar2 reduces the number of inner ear hair cells in zebrafish adults.
claims.source: We conclude that minar2 is required for mechanotransduction in the zebrafish larvae, and loss of minar2 reduces the number of inner ear hair cells in the zebrafish adults.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by hair cell counting data in adult zebrafish shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 is localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of the hair cell.
claims.source: We observed that GFP-Minar2 was localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of the hair cell, apparently around and just below the cuticular plate.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The GFP-Minar2 fluorescence co-localizes with phalloidin-labeled stereocilia.
claims.source: The GFP-Minar2 fluorescence co-localized with the phalloidin-labeled stereocilia (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization imaging shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: FLAG-Minar2 is localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of hair cells.
claims.source: The results showed that FLAG-Minar2 was similarly localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of hair cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 is localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of hair cells in the stable transgenic line.
claims.source: We subsequently generated a stable transgenic line using the myo6b:GFP-Minar2 construct and we found that GFP-Minar2 was also localized to the stereocilia and the apical region of the hair cells in the transgenic animals (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data from the transgenic line shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Prominent vesicle-like structures are seen below the cuticular plate in GFP-Minar2 expressing cells.
claims.source: Prominent vesicle-like structures were seen below the cuticular plate, while a ring-like structure was often observed at the base of the hair bundle.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of GFP-Minar2 distribution shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: A ring-like structure is often observed at the base of the hair bundle in GFP-Minar2 expressing cells.
claims.source: Prominent vesicle-like structures were seen below the cuticular plate, while a ring-like structure was often observed at the base of the hair bundle.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of GFP-Minar2 distribution shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: There is no observable GFP-Minar2 signal in the kinocilia.
claims.source: We co-labeled the kinocilia with anti-acetylated tubulin antibodies in the myo6b:GFP-Minar2 transgenic zebrafish and found there was no observable GFP-Minar2 signal in the kinocilia (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Hair bundles of inner ear hair cells are longer in the mutant minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 larvae.
claims.source: We labeled the hair bundles with phalloidin and observed that the hair bundles of inner ear hair cells were longer in the mutant minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 larvae (Figure 2C, for 5 dpf, wt: 4.77±0.06 μm, minar2fs139: 5.62±0.07 μm, minar2fs140: 5.15±0.07 μm, F(2, 847)=42.58, p<0.001; for 8 dpf, wt: 5.72±0.08 μm, minar2fs139: 6.80±0.09 μm, minar2fs140: 6.10±0.08 μm, F(2, 817)=42.95, p<0.001), and the hair bundles also appeared thinner.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by phalloidin staining and measurements shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Hair bundles appear thinner in the mutant minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 larvae.
claims.source: We labeled the hair bundles with phalloidin and observed that the hair bundles of inner ear hair cells were longer in the mutant minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 larvae (Figure 2C, for 5 dpf, wt: 4.77±0.06 μm, minar2fs139: 5.62±0.07 μm, minar2fs140: 5.15±0.07 μm, F(2, 847)=42.58, p<0.001; for 8 dpf, wt: 5.72±0.08 μm, minar2fs139: 6.80±0.09 μm, minar2fs140: 6.10±0.08 μm, F(2, 817)=42.95, p<0.001), and the hair bundles also appeared thinner.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of phalloidin-stained hair bundles shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The thinning and lengthening of mutant hair bundles are more pronounced in adult minar2fs139 mutants.
claims.source: The thinning and lengthening of the mutant hair bundles were more pronounced in adult minar2fs139 mutants (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by measurements in adult zebrafish shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: In 6-month-old adults, the average length of mutant hair bundles is more than 50% longer than that of wild type controls.
claims.source: In the 6-month-old adults, the average length of mutant hair bundles was more than 50% longer than that of wild type controls (wt: 3.77±0.11 μm, minar2fs139: 5.77±0.12 μm, t=12.05, df = 158, p<0.0001), and the width was only half that of the controls (wt: 1.66±0.05 μm, minar2fs139: 0.88±0.04 μm, t=12.65, df = 158, p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: In 6-month-old adults, the width of mutant hair bundles is only half that of wild type controls.
claims.source: In the 6-month-old adults, the average length of mutant hair bundles was more than 50% longer than that of wild type controls (wt: 3.77±0.11 μm, minar2fs139: 5.77±0.12 μm, t=12.05, df = 158, p<0.0001), and the width was only half that of the controls (wt: 1.66±0.05 μm, minar2fs139: 0.88±0.04 μm, t=12.65, df = 158, p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The kinocilia of lateral line hair cells are disorganized in the minar2 mutant larvae.
claims.source: We also found that the kinocilia of lateral line hair cells were disorganized in the minar2 mutant larvae, in contrast to the normal bundled together morphology in the wild-type animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, for 5 dpf, minar2fs139: p<0.001, minar2fs140: p<0.01; for 8 dpf, minar2fs139: p<0.001, minar2fs140: p<0.01. Fisher's exact test).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging and quantification shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The apical region of the hair cell is teeming with endocytotic vesicles, many of which are lysosomes.
claims.source: Previous electron microscopy and immunofluorescence microscopy studies showed that the apical region of the hair cell is teeming with endocytotic vesicles, many of which are lysosomes (Revelo et al., 2014; Spicer et al., 1999; Wiwatpanit et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Lamp1-GFP-positive lysosomes are abundantly distributed in the apical region of inner ear hair cells.
claims.source: Similar to the findings in the mouse model, we observed that Lamp1-GFP-positive lysosomes were abundantly distributed in the apical region of the inner ear hair cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Lamp1-GFP imaging data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: There are a few lysosomes distributed along the basolateral membrane of hair cells.
claims.source: There were also a few lysosomes distributed along the basolateral membrane of the hair cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of Lamp1-GFP distribution shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: In wild-type controls, most Lamp1-GFP labeled lysosomes are small sphere- or rod-shaped vesicles.
claims.source: In the wild-type controls, most of these Lamp1-GFP labeled lysosomes were small sphere- or rod-shaped vesicles.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of Lamp1-GFP distribution shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Large-sized Lamp1-GFP-labeled structures are occasionally observed in wild-type controls (in 39 out of 184 hair cells).
claims.source: Occasionally, rare and large-sized Lamp1-GFP-labeled structures were observed (in 39 out of 184 hair cells) and these structures likely were abnormally enlarged lysosomes or lysosome aggregates (diameter >2 μm).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of Lamp1-GFP structures shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Large round-shaped lysosomal structures (diameter >2 μm) are frequently observed in the inner ear hair cells of the minar2fs139 mutant (observed in 134 out of 236 hair cells).
claims.source: In contrast, in the inner ear hair cells of the minar2fs139 mutant, the large round-shaped lysosomal structures (diameter >2 μm) were frequently observed (observed in 134 out of 236 hair cells), and these abnormally enlarged lysosome aggregates were always located at the apical region of the hair cells (Figure 2E, p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Abnormally enlarged lysosome aggregates are always located at the apical region of hair cells in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: In contrast, in the inner ear hair cells of the minar2fs139 mutant, the large round-shaped lysosomal structures (diameter >2 μm) were frequently observed (observed in 134 out of 236 hair cells), and these abnormally enlarged lysosome aggregates were always located at the apical region of the hair cells (Figure 2E, p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of Lamp1-GFP distribution shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Abnormally enlarged lysosome aggregates are also observed in the hair cells of lateral line neuromasts in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: Similar results showing abnormally enlarged lysosome aggregates were also observed in the hair cells of the lateral line neuromasts (Figure 2F, p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Minar2 may play a role in regulating the apical lysosomes in hair cells.
claims.source: These data suggested that Minar2 may play a role in regulating the apical lysosomes in the hair cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of enlarged lysosomes in the minar2 mutant.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 signals partially overlap with Lamp1-mCherry signals at the apical region of inner ear hair cells.
claims.source: Consistent with this view, GFP-Minar2 signals partially overlapped with the Lamp1-mCherry signals at the apical region of the inner ear hair cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization imaging shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 most strongly co-localizes with lysosomes in cultured cells.
claims.source: We found GFP-Minar2 most strongly co-localized with lysosomes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization experiments with organelle markers shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C.

claims.claim: When the morphology and distribution of lysosomes are altered after U18666A treatment, GFP-Minar2 signals follow the changes of lysosomes.
claims.source: Furthermore, when the morphology and distribution of the lysosomes were altered after treatment with U18666A, GFP-Minar2 signals followed the changes of lysosomes, increased in the particle sizes, and accumulated toward the nuclear region (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging after U18666A treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 is localized on the lysosomal membranes.
claims.source: We further stained the lysosome lumen with filipin staining of cholesterol, which was trapped inside the lysosome after treatment with U18666A; and we observed that GFP-Minar2 signals appeared as circles that circumscribed the filipin signals, indicating GFP-Minar2 was localized on the lysosomal membranes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-staining experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: A conserved sequence pattern in Minar2 matches the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD).
claims.source: One of the conserved sequence patterns (π-S/T-Ω-S/T-Ψ-ζ-ζ-Ω) had 125 hits in the Metazoa [taxid:33208] proteins, and 37 out of the 125 hit sequences matched to Caveolin-1 protein from various species (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by protein pattern search results shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The matched sequence pattern resides in the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD).
claims.source: A close inspection revealed that the matched sequence pattern resided in the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD), which is known to interact with other proteins (Murata et al., 1995; Razani et al., 2002) and lipid membranes (Schlegel et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis and citations to studies on CSD function.

claims.claim: The CSD of caveolin is known to interact with other proteins.
claims.source: A close inspection revealed that the matched sequence pattern resided in the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD), which is known to interact with other proteins (Murata et al., 1995; Razani et al., 2002) and lipid membranes (Schlegel et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Murata et al., 1995 and Razani et al., 2002.

claims.claim: The CSD of caveolin is known to interact with lipid membranes.
claims.source: A close inspection revealed that the matched sequence pattern resided in the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD), which is known to interact with other proteins (Murata et al., 1995; Razani et al., 2002) and lipid membranes (Schlegel et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schlegel et al., 1999.

claims.claim: The CSD of caveolin directly binds to cholesterol in membranes.
claims.source: The CSD of caveolin also directly binds to cholesterol in the membranes (Ikonen et al., 2004; Liu et al., 2016; Murata et al., 1995) and this binding may contribute to the enrichment of cholesterol in the caveolae (Everson and Smart, 2005; Frank et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on caveolin-cholesterol binding.

claims.claim: CSD binding to cholesterol may contribute to the enrichment of cholesterol in caveolae.
claims.source: The CSD of caveolin also directly binds to cholesterol in the membranes (Ikonen et al., 2004; Liu et al., 2016; Murata et al., 1995) and this binding may contribute to the enrichment of cholesterol in the caveolae (Everson and Smart, 2005; Frank et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Everson and Smart, 2005 and Frank et al., 2006.

claims.claim: In cells expressing GFP-Minar2, filipin signals are accumulated in the perinuclear regions.
claims.source: In contrast, in cells expressing GFP-Minar2 fusion protein, the filipin signals were accumulated in the perinuclear regions and there were strong overlaps between the Minar2 and the filipin signals in the perinuclear regions (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by filipin staining data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: There are strong overlaps between Minar2 and filipin signals in the perinuclear regions.
claims.source: In contrast, in cells expressing GFP-Minar2 fusion protein, the filipin signals were accumulated in the perinuclear regions and there were strong overlaps between the Minar2 and the filipin signals in the perinuclear regions (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by filipin staining data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: There are significant increases of intracellular unesterified cholesterol in cells expressing GFP-Minar2.
claims.source: Quantification of the filipin signals revealed that there were significant increases of intracellular unesterified cholesterol in cells expressing GFP-Minar2 (total filipin fluorescence, for HEK293 cells, 79.0±3.0 au for GFP-only control, 106±3.8 au for GFP-Minar2 group, t=5.654, df = 104.6, p<0.0001; for Cos-7 cells, 100.5±8.2 au for GFP-only control, 140.3±12.9 au for GFP-Minar2 group, t=2.608, df = 55.73, p=0.012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of filipin staining shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 recruits filipin signals to where GFP signals are located.
claims.source: The quantification results also confirmed that GFP-Minar2 recruited the filipin signals to where GFP signals were located (recruited filipin intensity, for HEK293 cells, 5.85±0.51 au for GFP-only control, 23.56±1.36 au for GFP-Minar2 group, t=12.20, df = 72.42, p<0.0001; for Cos-7 cells, 12.08±1.1 au for GFP-only control, 22.14±2.31 au for GFP-Minar2 group, t=3.903, df = 48.96, p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of filipin recruitment shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Cholesterol in biological membranes is organized in three pools: a fixed pool for membrane integrity, a sequestered pool with low chemical activity, and an active/accessible pool with high activity.
claims.source: Previous studies suggested that cholesterol in the biological membranes is organized in three pools, a fixed pool for membrane integrity, a sequestered pool with low chemical activity, and an active/accessible pool with high activity (Das et al., 2014; Lange and Steck, 2016; Lange et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on cholesterol organization.

claims.claim: Protein probes derived from Perfringolysin O (PFO) and the D4 domain have been widely used to measure the accessible pool of cholesterol in biological membranes.
claims.source: Protein probes derived from the bacterial toxin Perfringolysin O (PFO) and the minimal cholesterol-binding domain 4 (D4 or D4H) of PFO have been widely used to measure the accessible pool of cholesterol in biological membranes (Das et al., 2014; Lim et al., 2019; Maekawa and Fairn, 2015; Naito et al., 2019; Schoop et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies using D4H probes.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 co-localizes with D4H-mCherry signals in cultured cells.
claims.source: Similar to what was observed in cells stained by filipin, GFP-Minar2 co-localized with D4H-mCherry signals, and recruited the D4H-mCherry signals to the perinuclear regions (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization imaging shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: GFP-Minar2 recruits D4H-mCherry signals to the perinuclear regions.
claims.source: Similar to what was observed in cells stained by filipin, GFP-Minar2 co-localized with D4H-mCherry signals, and recruited the D4H-mCherry signals to the perinuclear regions (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Minar2 co-localizes with cholesterol.
claims.source: We conclude that Minar2 co-localizes with cholesterol and that Minar2 may increase intracellular cholesterol levels when overexpressed in vitro.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data with filipin and D4H-mCherry shown in Figure 3B-C.

claims.claim: Minar2 may increase intracellular cholesterol levels when overexpressed in vitro.
claims.source: We conclude that Minar2 co-localizes with cholesterol and that Minar2 may increase intracellular cholesterol levels when overexpressed in vitro.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by filipin quantification data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Cholesterol levels are higher in the apical membranes than in the lateral wall membranes in isolated outer hair cells and fixed cochlear tissues.
claims.source: In isolated outer hair cells and outer hair cells in fixed cochlear tissues, cholesterol levels are higher in the apical membranes than those in the lateral wall membranes (Nguyen and Brownell, 1998; Takahashi et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nguyen and Brownell, 1998 and Takahashi et al., 2016.

claims.claim: The apical regions of inner ear hair cells show distinct filipin labeling.
claims.source: The apical regions of inner ear hair cells showed distinct filipin labeling (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by filipin staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry specifically labels the stereocilia when expressed in inner ear hair cells.
claims.source: Strikingly, when expressed in the inner ear hair cells by microinjection, D4H-mCherry specifically labeled the stereocilia regardless of its expression levels (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Low-intensity labeling of kinocilia is observed in cells with high levels of D4H-mCherry expression.
claims.source: Low-intensity labeling of kinocilia was also observed in cells with high levels of D4H-mCherry expression, while the basolateral membranes of hair cells were not or only very faintly labeled (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of D4H-mCherry distribution shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The basolateral membranes of hair cells are not or only very faintly labeled by D4H-mCherry.
claims.source: Low-intensity labeling of kinocilia was also observed in cells with high levels of D4H-mCherry expression, while the basolateral membranes of hair cells were not or only very faintly labeled (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of D4H-mCherry distribution shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: PM-GFP uniformly labels the basolateral membranes, stereocilia, and kinocilia membranes.
claims.source: As expected, PM-GFP uniformly labeled the basolateral membranes, together with the stereocilia and the kinocilia membranes (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The mean area of the stereocilium region is only 16.5 ± 0.1% of that of basolateral regions.
claims.source: The results showed that although the mean area of the stereocilium region was only 16.5 ± 0.1% of that of basolateral regions, the mean PM-GFP fluorescence within the stereocilium regions was 73.7 ± 4.0% of that of the basolateral regions.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The mean PM-GFP fluorescence within the stereocilium regions is 73.7 ± 4.0% of that of the basolateral regions.
claims.source: The results showed that although the mean area of the stereocilium region was only 16.5 ± 0.1% of that of basolateral regions, the mean PM-GFP fluorescence within the stereocilium regions was 73.7 ± 4.0% of that of the basolateral regions.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The mean D4H-mCherry fluorescence within the stereocilium regions is 567.7 ± 80.1% of that of the basolateral regions.
claims.source: Strikingly, the mean D4H-mCherry fluorescence within the stereocilium regions was 567.7 ± 80.1% of that of the basolateral regions, which was 7.7 times higher than that of PM-GFP (p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: There is an enrichment of D4H-mCherry in the stereocilium membrane over the basolateral membranes.
claims.source: Therefore, the disproportional distribution of D4H-mCherry in the stereocilium is much larger than what is expected from the distribution of the general plasma membrane probe PM-GFP, indicating that there was an enrichment of D4H-mCherry in the stereocilium membrane over the basolateral membranes.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing D4H-mCherry and PM-GFP distributions shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The D4HT490G-L491G variant does not bind cholesterol.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that the threonine–leucine pair in loop L1 of PFO domain 4 is essential for cholesterol recognition, and substitution of the T490-L491 pair with glycine residues abolishes cholesterol binding without perturbation of the overall structure of PFO (Farrand et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Farrand et al., 2010.

claims.claim: D4HT490G-L491G-mCherry gives rise to diffused signals in the cytoplasm only when expressed in hair cells.
claims.source: When the D4HT490G-L491G-mCherry variant was expressed in the hair cells, it gave rise to diffused signals in the cytoplasm only (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry labels stereocilia in lateral line neuromast hair cells.
claims.source: In the hair cells of the lateral line neuromasts, the stereocilia were similarly strongly labeled by D4H-mCherry.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: There are observable but weaker D4H-mCherry signals on the basolateral membranes of lateral line hair cells.
claims.source: There were also observable but weaker D4H-mCherry signals on the basolateral membranes of the lateral line hair cells (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of D4H-mCherry distribution shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: There are high levels of cholesterol located in the stereocilia membranes.
claims.source: These data suggested that there are high levels of cholesterol located in the stereocilia membranes, while the cholesterol levels are markedly lower in the basolateral membranes of the hair cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from D4H-mCherry distribution data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Cholesterol levels are markedly lower in the basolateral membranes of hair cells.
claims.source: These data suggested that there are high levels of cholesterol located in the stereocilia membranes, while the cholesterol levels are markedly lower in the basolateral membranes of the hair cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from D4H-mCherry distribution data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Both GFP-Minar2 and D4H-mCherry signals co-localize in the stereocilia.
claims.source: As expected, both GFP-Minar2 and D4H-mCherry signals co-localized in the stereocilia (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization imaging shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: There are abundant GFP-Minar2 signals just below the stereocilia and in the apical region of hair cells.
claims.source: Just below the stereocilia and in the apical region of hair cells, there were abundant GFP-Minar2 signals, and close inspections revealed a few D4H-mCherry-labeled structures that co-localized with GFP-Minar2 (Figure 4C insert).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: A few D4H-mCherry-labeled structures co-localize with GFP-Minar2 in the apical region.
claims.source: Just below the stereocilia and in the apical region of hair cells, there were abundant GFP-Minar2 signals, and close inspections revealed a few D4H-mCherry-labeled structures that co-localized with GFP-Minar2 (Figure 4C insert).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging shown in Figure 4C insert.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry additionally labels kinocilia, in which GFP-Minar2 signals are absent.
claims.source: D4H-mCherry additionally labeled kinocilia, in which GFP-Minar2 signals were absent.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Minar2 co-localizes with cholesterol in the stereocilia in vivo.
claims.source: Thus, similar to co-localization results in the cultured cells in vitro (Figure 3C), Minar2 co-localized with cholesterol in the stereocilia in vivo.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry still labels stereocilia in the hair cells of inner ears in the mutant minar2fs139 larvae.
claims.source: In the hair cells of the inner ears in the mutant minar2fs139 larvae, D4H-mCherry still labeled stereocilia (Figure 4D), but the intensities of the signals were dramatically reduced.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: The intensities of D4H-mCherry signals are dramatically reduced in the mutant minar2fs139 larvae.
claims.source: In the hair cells of the inner ears in the mutant minar2fs139 larvae, D4H-mCherry still labeled stereocilia (Figure 4D), but the intensities of the signals were dramatically reduced.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: The average D4H-mCherry signals of inner ear stereocilia in the minar2fs139 larvae are about half of those in wild controls.
claims.source: The results showed the average D4H-mCherry signals of inner ear stereocilia in the minar2fs139 larvae were about half of those in the wild controls (59.16 ± 5.92% and 56.62 ± 7.15% for 5 and 8 dpf, respectively).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: The expression levels of D4H-mCherry are similar between wild-type controls and mutant minar2fs139 larvae.
claims.source: The decreases were not due to changes in transgene expression either, since the western blotting results showed that the expression levels of D4H-mCherry were similar between the wild-type controls and the mutant minar2fs139 larvae (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: There is a similar reduction of D4H-mCherry signal in lateral line neuromast hair cells at 5 dpf.
claims.source: In the hair cells of lateral line neuromasts, there was a similar reduction of D4H-mCherry signal at 5 dpf (59.30 ± 5.98% of controls), while the signal intensity was no different from the wild-type controls at 8 dpf (121.39% of controls, n=41 and 44 for the wild type and the minar2fs139 mutant, respectively. t=0.8889, df = 83, p=0.3766).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry signal intensity is no different from wild-type controls at 8 dpf in lateral line neuromast hair cells.
claims.source: In the hair cells of lateral line neuromasts, there was a similar reduction of D4H-mCherry signal at 5 dpf (59.30 ± 5.98% of controls), while the signal intensity was no different from the wild-type controls at 8 dpf (121.39% of controls, n=41 and 44 for the wild type and the minar2fs139 mutant, respectively. t=0.8889, df = 83, p=0.3766).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry labels many large, round- and rod-shaped vesicles in the cell body regions of neuromast hair cells in the minar2fs139 mutant at 8 dpf.
claims.source: While D4H-mCherry primarily labeled the stereocilia membranes in both wild-type controls and the minar2fs139 mutant at 5 dpf, D4H-mCherry labeled many large, round- and rod-shaped vesicles in the cell body regions of the neuromast hair cells in the minar2fs139 mutant at 8 dpf (Figure 4E, p<0.01, Fisher's exact test).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging and quantification shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: D4H-mCherry-labeled large vesicles in the hair cells of minar2fs139 mutant likely correspond to enlarged lysosomes.
claims.source: These D4H-mCherry-labeled large vesicles in the hair cells of minar2fs139 mutant likely corresponded to enlarged lysosomes, as these abnormal vesicles were co-labeled by the lysosome probe Lamp1-GFP, but not by the plasma membrane probe PM-GFP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from co-labeling experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: There are significant increases in relative mRNA expression for Srebp2 target genes hmgcr and hmgcs1 in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: We found that there were significant increases in relative mRNA expression for Srebp2 target genes hmgcr (2.6±0.2 fold) and hmgcs1 (1.7±0.2 fold) in the minar2fs139 mutant, while expression levels of LXR target gene abcg1 and mylip were not changed (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Expression levels of LXR target genes abcg1 and mylip are not changed in the minar2fs139 mutant.
claims.source: We found that there were significant increases in relative mRNA expression for Srebp2 target genes hmgcr (2.6±0.2 fold) and hmgcs1 (1.7±0.2 fold) in the minar2fs139 mutant, while expression levels of LXR target gene abcg1 and mylip were not changed (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: The sterol synthesis pathway is activated due to a reduction of the accessible cholesterol pool in the minar2fs139 mutant larvae.

claims.source: Our previous study showed that Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor acts as a negative regulator of mTOR signaling through its interaction with the Deptor protein, an integral component of the mTORC complex (Zhang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Loss of the ubtor gene in zebrafish causes motor hyperactivity and epilepsy-like behaviors by elevating neuronal activity and activating mTOR signaling.
claims.source: Loss of the ubtor gene in zebrafish causes motor hyperactivity and epilepsy-like behaviors by elevating neuronal activity and activating mTOR signaling (Wang et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Ubtor/MINAR1 plays a role in angiogenesis and breast cancer.
claims.source: It has also been shown that Ubtor/MINAR1 plays a role in angiogenesis and breast cancer (Ho et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ho et al., 2018.

claims.claim: The region in Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor that interacts with the Deptor protein is missing in the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein.
claims.source: Since the region in Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor that interacts with the Deptor protein is missing in the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein, the regulation of mTOR signaling is likely a function specific to the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on protein sequence comparison.

claims.claim: The cholesterol-binding region identified in this study is conserved in the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
claims.source: Because the cholesterol-binding region that we identify in this study is conserved in the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein, it should be interesting to investigate whether Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor also plays a role in the regulation of cholesterol.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claims.claim: The human ortholog MINAR2 is specifically expressed by the auditory hair cells.
claims.source: Because of the conserved requirement of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 gene orthologs for hearing in both mice and zebrafish, and that the human ortholog MINAR2 is also specifically expressed by the auditory hair cells (Steinhart et al., 2022), it will be important to examine whether KIAA1024L/MINAR2 gene mutations may underline hearing abnormalities in humans.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steinhart et al., 2022.

claims.claim: Mutations in MINAR2 cause deafness in human patients.
claims.source: Indeed, while this study was under review, it was reported that mutations in MINAR2 cause deafness in human patients (Bademci et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bademci et al., 2022.

results.result: Disruption of kiaa1024L/minar2 causes hearing loss in zebrafish larvae, as demonstrated by reduced C-start response rates and elevated auditory evoked potential (AEP) thresholds.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C62-C65 provide converging evidence from two independent hearing assays (C-start response and AEP recordings) showing significant hearing deficits in minar2fs139 mutants. The statistical analyses are appropriate (Mann-Whitney test for C-start, two-way repeated-measures ANOVA for AEP) with significant p-values reported. The data demonstrate both behavioral and electrophysiological hearing impairment.

results.result: Loss of minar2 function primarily affects mechanotransduction in hair cells, as shown by reduced AM1-43 labeling that exceeds the reduction in hair cell numbers.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C67, and C69 demonstrate that AM1-43 labeling is reduced by ~50% while hair cell numbers decrease by only ~18%. The inference that mechanotransduction is primarily affected (C69) is logically sound given the disproportionate reduction in AM1-43 uptake relative to cell loss. Statistical significance is demonstrated with appropriate tests.

results.result: Hair bundles in minar2 mutants are significantly longer and thinner than wild-type controls, with phenotypes becoming more pronounced in adults.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C85-C89 provide quantitative measurements of hair bundle morphology at multiple developmental stages (5 dpf, 8 dpf, 6 months) using phalloidin staining. Statistical analyses show significant differences (p<0.001) with appropriate tests (ANOVA, t-tests). The progressive nature of the phenotype is well-documented, with adult mutants showing >50% increase in length and 50% reduction in width.

results.result: Enlarged apical lysosomes are frequently observed in minar2 mutant hair cells, with abnormally large lysosomal structures (>2 μm diameter) present in the majority of mutant inner ear hair cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C95-C98 demonstrate a striking phenotype using Lamp1-GFP labeling. The quantification shows enlarged lysosomes in 134/236 mutant hair cells versus 39/184 wild-type cells (p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test). The consistent localization to the apical region and replication in both inner ear and lateral line neuromasts strengthens the finding.

results.result: Cholesterol is highly enriched in hair bundle membranes, as demonstrated by D4H-mCherry probe distribution showing 7.7-fold higher enrichment in stereocilia compared to basolateral membranes relative to a general plasma membrane probe.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C122, C126-C129, and C134 provide strong evidence for cholesterol enrichment using the D4H-mCherry cholesterol probe compared to PM-GFP plasma membrane control. The quantitative analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) shows D4H-mCherry fluorescence in stereocilia is 567.7±80.1% of basolateral levels, which is 7.7 times higher than PM-GFP distribution (p<0.0001). The use of a non-binding D4HT490G-L491G control (C131) validates probe specificity.

results.result: Loss of kiaa1024L/minar2 reduces cholesterol localization to hair bundles, with D4H-mCherry signals in mutant stereocilia reduced to approximately 50-60% of wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C141-C143, and C145 demonstrate reduced cholesterol in mutant hair bundles using the D4H-mCherry probe. Quantification shows consistent ~50% reduction in inner ear hair cells at both 5 and 8 dpf, with similar reduction in lateral line at 5 dpf. Western blot controls (C144) confirm equal transgene expression, ruling out expression differences as a confound.

results.result: Lowering cholesterol levels with 2HPβCD aggravates hair cell defects in minar2 mutants, mimicking and exacerbating the mutant phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C10, C153-C154, C156, C159-C160 demonstrate that 2HPβCD treatment reduces cholesterol (to 16.5% of control) and mechanotransduction (AM1-43 to 33.5% of control) in wild-type, and further reduces both measures in mutants to levels similar to treated wild-type. The additive effect supports a model where minar2 and cholesterol depletion act through related mechanisms. Statistical significance is demonstrated throughout.

results.result: Increasing cholesterol levels with efavirenz rescues hair cell defects and hearing in minar2 mutants, restoring D4H-mCherry signals, AM1-43 labeling, and C-start responses to wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C169, C171-C173, C177-C178 provide strong rescue evidence. Efavirenz treatment increases D4H-mCherry from 55.8±7.0% to 88.7±8.4% (p=0.021) and AM1-43 from 61.8±2.9% to 96.1±3.1% (p<0.0001) in mutants, with both restored to wild-type levels (p>0.1). C-start responses are also rescued (C177). The specificity is supported by voriconazole replication (C175-C176).

results.result: GFP- or FLAG-tagged Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein localizes to stereocilia and apical endo-membranes in hair cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C40, C78-C81 demonstrate consistent localization using multiple approaches: transient expression of GFP-Minar2 (C78-C79), FLAG-Minar2 (C80), and stable transgenic line (C81). The co-localization with phalloidin-labeled stereocilia (C79) and absence from kinocilia (C84) provide spatial specificity. Multiple independent constructs and imaging approaches strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is mainly localized to lysosomes in cultured cells, specifically on lysosomal membranes.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C41, C101-C103 demonstrate lysosomal localization through co-localization with Lyso-Tracker Red (highest Pearson's r=0.836 in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), tracking with lysosomes after U18666A treatment (C102), and circumscribing filipin-stained lysosomal cholesterol (C103). The membrane localization inference (C103) is supported by the spatial relationship to filipin signals.

results.result: Overexpression of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 in cultured cells recruits cholesterol to perinuclear regions and increases total intracellular cholesterol levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C42, C110-C113 demonstrate that GFP-Minar2 overexpression increases total filipin fluorescence (HEK293: 79.0±3.0 to 106±3.8 au, p<0.0001; Cos-7: 100.5±8.2 to 140.3±12.9 au, p=0.012) and recruits filipin to GFP-positive regions (HEK293: 5.85±0.51 to 23.56±1.36 au, p<0.0001). Similar results with D4H-mCherry probe (C116-C117) support cholesterol recruitment.

results.result: The sterol synthesis pathway is activated in minar2fs139 mutants, as evidenced by upregulation of Srebp2 target genes hmgcr and hmgcs1, while LXR target genes remain unchanged.
results.evaluation: Claims C149-C151 show significant upregulation of Srebp2 targets (hmgcr: 2.6±0.2 fold; hmgcs1: 1.7±0.2 fold) with no change in LXR targets (abcg1, mylip) by qRT-PCR. The selective activation of Srebp2 pathway is consistent with reduced accessible cholesterol pool (C151), though this inference relies on established cholesterol homeostasis mechanisms.

results.result: Point mutations of critical aromatic residues (Y/W) in CRAC/CARC motifs of MINAR2 compromise cholesterol recruitment and intracellular cholesterol labeling in cultured cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C179-C183 demonstrate that MINAR2YW-A mutations reduce recruited filipin (24.58±1.30 to 14.85±0.90 au, p<0.0001) and total filipin (103.9±4.86 to 86.43±3.21 au, p<0.01) without affecting expression levels (C183). This supports direct cholesterol interaction through CRAC/CARC motifs, though direct binding assays would strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: Computational docking analysis identifies the conserved CSD-matching sequence as the cholesterol binding site with best binding free energy (−8.1 kJ/mol), involving mutated aromatic residues W112 and Y117.
results.evaluation: Claims C184-C185 provide computational support for the cholesterol binding site using AlphaFold2 structure and AutoDock. The binding free energy (−8.1 kJ/mol) is reasonable for protein-lipid interactions, and the involvement of W112 and Y117 is consistent with mutagenesis results (C181-C182). However, computational docking has limitations and experimental binding assays would be needed for definitive proof.

results.result: Loss of minar2 reduces hair cell numbers in adult zebrafish inner ears but not in larvae, with progressive hair cell loss affecting utricles and saccules.
results.evaluation: Claims C68, C70, C73-C75, C77 demonstrate no change in larval inner ear hair cells (5 and 8 dpf, p>0.25) but significant reduction in adults (71.2-84.3% of wild-type, p<0.001). The progressive nature is well-documented, though the mechanism underlying the developmental timing difference is not explained. Lateral line shows ~18% reduction even in larvae (C68).

results.result: Minar2 co-localizes with cholesterol in stereocilia in vivo, as demonstrated by co-expression of GFP-Minar2 and D4H-mCherry in transgenic zebrafish.
results.evaluation: Claims C136-C138, C140 show co-localization of GFP-Minar2 and D4H-mCherry in stereocilia and some apical structures. The in vivo co-localization is consistent with in vitro results (C116-C117) and supports a functional relationship between Minar2 and cholesterol in hair bundles. The absence of Minar2 in kinocilia where D4H labels (C139) provides spatial specificity.

results.result: U18666A treatment, which traps cholesterol in lysosomes, reduces accessible cholesterol and mechanotransduction, with additive effects in minar2 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C162-C166 show U18666A reduces D4H-mCherry (to 50.2±4.6%) and AM1-43 labeling similarly to 2HPβCD, despite causing cholesterol accumulation in lysosomes (C161). The additive effect in mutants (C165-C166) suggests minar2 and U18666A affect overlapping but not identical processes. The altered D4H distribution (C163) supports lysosomal cholesterol trapping.

results.result: Efavirenz and voriconazole treatment rescue abnormally enlarged vesicles and abnormal D4H-mCherry distribution in minar2 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C174-C176 demonstrate that CYP46A1 inhibitors rescue cellular phenotypes beyond just cholesterol levels and mechanotransduction. The rescue of enlarged vesicles (C174) and D4H distribution (C176) with two independent inhibitors strengthens the conclusion that increasing cholesterol levels addresses multiple aspects of the mutant phenotype.

results.result: Cholesterol plays an essential role in hair bundles, and Kiaa1024L/Minar2 regulates cholesterol distribution and homeostasis to ensure normal hearing.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C13, C186-C187 represent the main conclusions synthesizing multiple lines of evidence: cholesterol enrichment in hair bundles (C8), reduced cholesterol in mutants (C9), pharmacological manipulation effects (C10-C11), and Minar2 localization (C40). The convergence of genetic, pharmacological, and localization data strongly supports this model, though the precise molecular mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.

results.result: Kiaa1024L/minar2 gene orthologs are found only in vertebrates and belong to the UPF0258 gene family, with zebrafish having one minar2 ortholog and two minar1/ubtor orthologs.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C48 are supported by phylogenetic analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and genome database searches. The vertebrate-specific distribution is clearly demonstrated, and the gene family classification is supported by citations. The genome annotation data for zebrafish orthologs appears reliable.

results.result: minar2 orthologs are highly enriched in auditory hair cells across species, including mouse, zebrafish, and human inner ear organoids.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C50 are supported by analysis of published sequencing datasets and in situ hybridization (C39, Figure 1A). The expression pattern is consistent across multiple species and datasets, strengthening the conclusion that minar2 has a conserved hair cell-specific function. The human organoid data (C50) extends relevance to human biology.

results.result: The minar2fs139 and minar2fs140 alleles are frameshift mutations causing premature termination and loss of the transmembrane helix, representing loss-of-function alleles.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C58 provide detailed molecular characterization of the mutant alleles. The 5 bp deletion/insertion causing frameshift and premature termination is well-documented by sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C). The prediction that truncated proteins lack the C-terminal transmembrane helix is sound, and the loss-of-function designation is supported by mRNA degradation (C59-C60).

results.result: minar2 expression is markedly down-regulated in both mutants, likely due to nonsense-mediated mRNA decay triggered by premature termination.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C60 are supported by qPCR data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) showing significant mRNA reduction. The inference of nonsense-mediated decay (C60) is reasonable given the premature stop codons, though this mechanism was not directly tested. The down-regulation strengthens the loss-of-function interpretation.

results.result: Expression levels of minar1a and minar1b are unchanged in minar2 mutants, indicating no genetic compensation by upregulation of related family members.
results.evaluation: Claim C61 is supported by qPCR data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) showing no significant changes in minar1a/b expression. This addresses a potential confound of genetic compensation, though compensation through other genes cannot be ruled out. The lack of compensation by closely related family members strengthens the specificity of the minar2 phenotype.

results.result: Kinocilia of lateral line hair cells are disorganized in minar2 mutant larvae.
results.evaluation: Claim C90 is supported by imaging and quantification (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) showing significant disorganization at both 5 and 8 dpf (p<0.01-0.001, Fisher's exact test). While this phenotype is documented, its relationship to the primary cholesterol/hair bundle defects is unclear and may represent a secondary consequence.

results.result: At 8 dpf, D4H-mCherry labels large vesicles in lateral line neuromast hair cells of minar2 mutants, which correspond to enlarged lysosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C148 show abnormal D4H-mCherry distribution at 8 dpf (p<0.01) with large vesicles co-labeled by Lamp1-GFP but not PM-GFP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D). The inference that these are enlarged lysosomes (C148) is well-supported by the co-labeling data. This connects the cholesterol and lysosome phenotypes.

results.result: Both 2HPβCD and U18666A cause small reductions in hair cell numbers in wild-type, but only U18666A further reduces hair cell numbers in minar2 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C167-C168 are supported by hair cell counting (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B). The differential effects of the two drugs on hair cell survival in mutants suggest distinct mechanisms beyond simple cholesterol depletion. However, the biological significance of this difference is not fully explored.

results.result: Homozygous minar2 mutants are viable with normal body length and weight in adults.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C72 are supported by measurements (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B). This indicates the phenotype is relatively specific to the auditory system rather than causing systemic developmental defects, which is important for interpreting the hearing-specific role of minar2.

results.result: A conserved sequence pattern in Minar2 matches the caveolin scaffolding domain (CSD), which is known to interact with cholesterol.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 are supported by protein pattern search results (Figure 3A) showing 37/125 hits matching Caveolin-1. The sequence similarity to CSD is documented, and the known cholesterol-binding properties of CSD (C106-C109) provide a mechanistic hypothesis. However, sequence similarity alone does not prove functional equivalence.

results.result: Loss of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 causes profound deafness in mice, as identified in genetic screens using auditory brainstem response testing.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C37-C38, C195 are supported by citations to Bowl et al., 2017 and Ingham et al., 2019. These prior studies provide the foundation for the current work. The claims accurately represent the cited work, establishing the importance of studying minar2 function.

results.result: minar2 orthologs play essential roles in auditory function across vertebrates, as demonstrated by hearing loss in both mice and zebrafish.
results.evaluation: Claims C66 and C196 synthesize evidence from both zebrafish (current study) and mouse (cited studies). The conservation of hearing loss phenotype across species strongly supports an essential and conserved role for minar2 in vertebrate hearing. This cross-species validation is a strength of the work.

results.result: Hearing loss in zebrafish minar2 mutants is less severe than in mouse knockouts and shows progressive hair cell loss from larval to adult stages.
results.evaluation: Claims C201-C203 compare phenotypes across species and developmental stages. The progressive nature in zebrafish (no larval inner ear hair cell loss but 30% reduction in adults) is well-documented. The comparison to mouse (C202, citing Bademci et al., 2022) is appropriate, though species differences in hair cell regeneration (C204-C205) may explain phenotypic differences.

results.result: The human ortholog MINAR2 is specifically expressed in auditory hair cells, and mutations in MINAR2 cause deafness in human patients.
results.evaluation: Claims C230-C231 extend the findings to human relevance. C230 is supported by citation to Steinhart et al., 2022, and C231 cites Bademci et al., 2022 showing human mutations cause deafness. This validates the translational relevance of the zebrafish model and suggests MINAR2 as a candidate gene for human hereditary hearing loss.
